title: penstemon jamesii subsp. typicus
intro: Penstemon jamesii subsp. typicus, commonly known as James' beardtongue, is a perennial plant species native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It belongs to the plantain family (Plantaginaceae) and is valued for its medicinal properties and ornamental value. The plant has been used to treat various health issues, including respiratory problems, due to its expectorant properties, which help loosen and clear mucus from the lungs, and its anti-inflammatory actions, which can soothe irritated tissues. The bioactive constituents of James' beardtongue include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other compounds that contribute to its therapeutic effects.
